Aditya Birla Health Activ One MAX vs SBI General Super Health Platinum Infinite

Side by side on the figures that decide a claim — and which one we would actually pick.

We score Aditya Birla Health Activ One MAX higher at 4.4/5 against 4.1/5, winning 4 of the 9 comparable measures. Activ One MAX is the cheaper of the two on the illustrated profiles.

Side by side

Highlighted cells are the better value on that row. Text rows are shown without a winner — deciding that one wording beats another is a judgement, not a measurement.
Measure Aditya Birla Health Activ One MAX SBI General Super Health Platinum Infinite

Activ One MAX

The best value on this list, and by a clear margin. It undercuts every other plan at every profile while holding a 96.25% settlement ratio, and the 500% cumulative bonus means the cover you buy at 28 is worth several times as much by 40. The caveats are that restoration starts from your second claim rather than your first, and that maternity is not available at all. If you are young, reasonably healthy and not planning a pregnancy in the next few years, this is where your money goes furthest.

Against it

  • 18.67 complaints per 10,000 claims — twice HDFC ERGO, though far better than Care Health
  • Restoration only kicks in from the second claim, not the first
  • Hitting the full 100% HealthReturns discount is very hard in practice
  • Maternity requires an entirely separate policy
  • A younger health insurer, so the servicing track record is shorter

Super Health Platinum Infinite

The most feature-complete plan on this list and, unavoidably, the most expensive. The two features worth paying for are the 2-year pre-existing disease wait and restoration from the first claim — both directly reduce the odds of a claim being declined in the early years. That combination makes it worth a serious look if you are covering parents with existing conditions, where the third waiting year is a genuine risk. For a healthy 25-year-old it is dramatic overkill; Activ One MAX does the job for a quarter of the price.

Against it

  • By far the most expensive — ₹45,944 for a 25-year-old, over four times Activ One MAX
  • The ₹50 lakh minimum base cover forces you into a large policy whether you want one or not
  • Global cover and the Health Multiplier are restricted to listed conditions only
  • Renewal discounts are tied to step counts, which will not suit everyone
  • Note that the premiums shown are at ₹50 lakh cover, not the ₹15 lakh used for the others

Which one we would pick

Aditya Birla Health Activ One MAX, on balance — 4.4/5 against 4.1/5. Where Activ One MAX is ahead: myinsurancebro score, claim settlement ratio, premium — couple, 31 & 32, premium — seniors, 62 & 63. Where Super Health Platinum Infinite is ahead: complaints per 10,000 claims, cashless hospitals, annual health premium, pre-existing disease wait, specific illness wait.

A score ranks plans on the evidence available; it cannot know your health history, your dependants or which exclusion will matter to you in ten years. Where the two are close, the deciding factor is usually the text rows above — room rent, waiting periods, exclusions — read against your own circumstances.

Scores are plan features 45%, insurer strength 45%, premium 10% — how we score plans.
